CINE 2014.title: AI in Filmmaking
CINE 2014.description: Introduces students to emerging artificial intelligence tools and their expanding role in contemporary filmmaking. Students explore how AI is reshaping story development, visualization, sound and image generation, editing, and production workflows. Through the production of self‑paced creative artifacts and critical analysis, students gain foundational literacy in AI‑assisted media creation while examining the historical, theoretical, and ethical dimensions of AI in cinema. No prior filmmaking or technical experience required.

CINE 2054.title: Introduction to Cinema
CINE 2054.description: Introduction to cinema as a medium for artistic communication. Interpretation and analysis of films to understand designs, ideas and values in artistic and cultural contexts. Basic elements of cinema structure and cinema terminology, phases of cinema production, cinema style of individual directors, creative work of cinematography, production design, and editing, ideological and social meaning in cinema, demographics of visual representation, cinemas economic marketplace. Ethical values and conflicts as found in given films, and ethical reasoning as part of the analysis of cinema.

CINE 2064.title: Cinema Production Foundations
CINE 2064.description: Foundational cinema production course. Hands-on introduction to camera operation, cinematic sound design, lighting, and digital editing. Emphasizes fiction and non-fiction storytelling, aesthetic principles, and collaborative and responsible filmmaking. Design Lab Studio.

CINE 2144.title: Topics Exploring Cinema Studies
CINE 2144.description: Examination of motion pictures and related media as expressive forms that shape and reflect human experience. Course topics vary by semester and may include themes such as sports and cinema, identity and representation, or media and technology. Students apply introductory concepts and methods of film and media analysis to specific case studies and interpret visual storytelling through aesthetic, cultural, critical, theoretical, and ethical perspectives. They also communicate informed, evidence-based arguments about cinema through writing and discussion. Designed for students across disciplines seeking a topics-based introduction to cinema as a humanistic field of study. May be repeated 2 times with different content for a maximum of 9 credit hours.

CINE 2184.title: Topics in Cinema Production
CINE 2184.description: Hands-on filmmaking course open to all undergraduates, emphasizing mindful practice and collaborative problem-solving. Focuses on visual communication, adaptive storytelling, field recording in uncontrolled environments, sound design, and project management through short-form film production. No prior experience required. This course may be repeated 2 times for a total of 9 credits.

CINE 2424.title: Fundamentals of Directing
CINE 2424.description: This course introduces key theories and practical methods for directing theatre and cinema. Students will develop skills in analysis of dramatic texts from a director’s perspective, develop and express a creative vision, and tackle directing challenges such as composition, directing actors, leadership of group creativity, and integration of design elements. Students will experiment with and apply visual and sonic storytelling skills as a director, give and receive constructive feedback utilizing critical response techniques, and gain knowledge of basic professional practices for a director in theatre and cinema. Design Lab Studio.

CINE 3144.title: Topics in Cinema & Humanities
CINE 3144.description: Applications of academic humanities methodologies (critical theory, cultural studies, historical analysis) to understand the cinema. Compare and contrast various academic humanities methodologies as they pertain to an understanding of the aesthetic, history, and theory of cinema. Write and speak intelligently about the cinema's relationship to the humanities. Readings in the disciplines of architecture, studio arts, music, theater, literature, and others. May be repeated 2 times with different content for a maximum of 9 credit hours.

CINE 3184.title: Cinema Production Topics
CINE 3184.description: Rotating topics in cinema production. Designed for majors in the Department of Theatre and Cinema who have foundational training in areas of cinema production. May be repeated for credit with different course content up to a maximum of nine credit hours.

CINE 3214.title: Fiction Cinema Production
CINE 3214.description: Intermediate-level fiction film production course. Foundational cinema production skills, dramatic storytelling techniques, intermediate directing, team- based ownership and responsibility, and project management.

CINE 3224.title: Documentary Cinema Production
CINE 3224.description: Intermediate-level, non-fiction, film production course for students seeking non-fiction documentary film production skills and experience. Emphasizes the application and advancement of foundational skills, the ethics of documentary filmmaking, story development and project management.

CINE 3534.title: Avant-Garde Cinema
CINE 3534.description: Close visual and cultural study of the avant-garde and experimental tradition in the first half-century of American and European cinemas; emphasis on interrelations of cinema with avant-garde movements in other arts, including literature, music, dance, theatre, painting, and photography

CINE 3544.title: Literature and Cinema
CINE 3544.description: Works of literature and the films into which they have been transformed; emphasis on differences between media.

CINE 3900.title: Bridge Experience
CINE 3900.description: Application of academic knowledge and skills in a work-based experience aligned with post-graduation goals using research-based learning processes. Satisfactory completion of work-based experience often in the form of internship, undergraduate research, co-op, or study abroad; self-evaluation; reflection; and showcase of learning. Pre: Department approval of 3900 plan.

CINE 4144.title: Topics in Cinema Studies
CINE 4144.description: Critical issues in cinema. Aesthetic, social, political, and economic contexts for films that embody or critique assumptions of historical periods. Analysis of ethnocentric and cultural biases in cinema. Identifying issues of identity and equity in films. Theories and ethics of representation. May be repeated 2 times with different content for a maximum of 9 credits.

CINE 4154.title: Quantitative Research Methods for Cinema Studies
CINE 4154.description: This course introduces students to the application of quantitative thinking to the study of cinema. Through hands-on research and analysis, students will learn to frame questions, design solutions, and interpret data related to filmmaking practices and audience behaviors. Students will learn about various research paradigms, and how to choose methodologies based on what questions they would like to answer. Emphasis is placed on applying foundational quantitative principles to use various sampling techniques to gather data, evaluate evidence, draw valid inferences, and critically assess conclusions about media practices and effects. Students will also explore the challenges of studying human behavior within diverse historical and cultural contexts, developing skills to navigate uncertainty while producing meaningful insights.
